title: Continuous batching: admission & batch‑shape heuristics to cut decode tail latency
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: In mixed prefill+decode workloads we see occasional decode tail spikes (p95/p99) when large prefill requests collide with many short decode requests. Existing continuous-batcher yields high utilization but permits poorly shaped batches that cause head-of-line blocking and KV cache pressure.

Goal: Implement an adaptive admission/gating layer and batch-shaping heuristics that: (1) prevent large prefills from monopolizing GPU execution windows, (2) allow small decode-heavy traffic to be grouped into low-latency micro-batches, and (3) expose knobs for kernel-selection guidance when shapes are skewed. Target is 30-40% reduction in p99 decode latency under mixed workloads without regressions in throughput for sustained loads.

Scope: design and implement admission controller (token- and headroom-based), batch-shape-aware packer (favor homogeneous length/sequence groups), prefill-aware scheduling (de-prioritize long prefills or schedule them to dedicated time-slices), and light-weight heuristics to suggest kernel variants (FP16 vs quantized path) based on batch composition. Also add metrics and rollout for canary traffic.

Out of scope: full model re-compilation, deep kernel auto-tuner (follow-up task).
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency for mixed prefill+decode benchmark reduced by >=20% and p99 reduced by >=30% compared to baseline (same traffic profile)
No more than 5% throughput regression on sustained high-throughput workloads (95% CI)
New admission/gating config defaults safe for hosted customers and can be toggled per-customer in Dedicated/Private
End-to-end CI tests for continuous-batcher validate fair-pacing across prefills and decodes
Canary rollout plan and dashboard showing tail-latency, batch-shape distribution, and kernel path selection per model
implementation_notes: Admission controller: implement token-bucket with headroom reservation for decode-priority traffic and an override for SLA-tagged requests (customer tier)
Batch packer: add length-clustering pass before packing; prefer groups where (max_len/min_len) <= 2 to reduce padding waste and kernel divergence
Prefill scheduling: detect large prefill requests (>X tokens) and either route to a separate GPU queue or schedule in deferred burst windows when decode queue is low
Kernel hints: annotate batch meta with suggested execution path (quantized/FP16/mixed) based on per-model profile and batch shape; runtime uses hint to select kernel but falls back to safe default
Metrics: emit batch_shape histogram, admission_decisions counters, queue_wait_seconds percentiles, and kernel_path chosen labels to tracing
Rollout: feature-flag gated, start with 5% canary traffic (internal), expand to 25% then 100% after 72h stable metrics
Tests: unit tests for packer heuristics, integration harness to replay production trace with mix of short decodes and long prefills
benchmarks: Baseline (A100 40GB, mixed trace): p95 decode=420ms, p99 decode=1.2s, sustained throughput=1200 tokens/s
Spike experiment (admission + shaping): p95 decode=310ms (-26%), p99 decode=760ms (-37%), sustained throughput=1180 tokens/s
Model samples: redwood-alpha-7b and open-llama-13b, sequence mix 80% decoding short (<=40 tokens) and 20% large prefill (>512 tokens)
Memory: observed 8-12% lower temporary KV cache churn when batch-shaping engaged
